title: Vendor acceptance, security, and pricing alignment - StratusPay
summary: Procurement/legal sync where Redwood AE+SE walked through MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, and KMS/SSO options for a Dedicated vs Private deployment decision. Customer flagged SOC2 attestation, on-prem keying, and pricing approval path through FinOps. Agreed next steps: share redline-friendly MSA, SOC2 report, and an estimated pricing worksheet for a 90-day pilot with dedicated capacity.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (StratusPay Procurement), Derek Holt (StratusPay Security), Marco Silva (StratusPay Legal), Nina Oberoi (StratusPay Cloud), Priya Rao (StratusPay FinOps)

--- Auto summary present ---

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intro, i'm Maya Patel, AE on the account, joined by Liam our solutions eng. we wanted to make sure we hit the legal proc points, kms/ssO questions, and pricing pathway so you can get procurement moving.
[00:22] Aisha (StratusPay): Hi -- thanks, Maya. we have a pretty tight window this quarter, FinOps wants a pilot approved by mid April. so we need clarity on the MSA redlines and the pricing sheets.
[00:35] Maya: totally. we'll run through the MSA high level and note the items we've seen typically come up. Liam will cover the infra and keying options.
[00:42] Liam (Redwood): morning all. i'll try to keep it concrete. for the things you'll care about: customer-managed KMS (HSM options), SSO/SAML, and whether you go Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, or Redwood Private - those change the SLA and the key custody model.
[01:05] Derek (Security): quick interruption — when you say Dedicated vs Private, can you restate the key differences re: data plane and key custody? we've got auditors who want physical separation on desk.
[01:18] Liam: sure. Dedicated is our reserved GPU pool, logically isolated and single-tenant from a scheduling/compute perspective, but keys for encryption still live in Redwood's KMS unless you opt for customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations. Private (VPC/on-prem) means the control plane is routed through your VPC and you can run with customer HSM or a bring-your-own-key model. some customers call that on-prem-keying, others say 'private keying'. apologies for the naming mismatch — transcripts sometimes show Red wood Inferance or the Redwood Dedicate, so i try to repeat.
[02:05] Marco (Legal): on the MSA, our main asks: liability caps for trained model leakage, data retention terms in the DPA, and specific SLA remedies for downtime. do you typically accept a 12 month warranty period in section 7?
[02:22] Maya: we can be flexible on warranty, but liability caps are often a negotiation point. we've had enterprise customers accept a tiered cap tied to fees paid over 12 months. we'll flag examples in the redline tracker.
[02:35] Priya (FinOps): pricing wise: we need a clear pilot rate that doesn't surprise — token billing, embedding units, and any per-instance reserved fees. can you give an example for a 3-node dedicated pilot with mid-GPU (a100-ish) type?
[02:52] Liam: yes. for a reserved 3-node pool we typically present committed monthly pricing plus an overage/burst rate. i'll put numbers in the worksheet. note egress and KV cache sizing impact costs — small prefix caching reduces token spend but increases memory usage.
[03:20] Aisha: also SOC2 and pen test reports. procurement won't advance without attestation.
[03:28] Maya: understood, we'll upload SOC2 Type II and the latest pen test summary. our security team will redact IP but provide auditors with the required attestation.
[03:38] Derek: KMS specifics: do you support customer key rotation schedules and do you permit HSMs hosted in our cloud account? we want a true BYOK experience.
[03:50] Liam: yes to rotation schedules; we integrate with common KMS providers and HSMs. caveat: if you run in Hosted, keys are wrapped via our gateway unless you run a Private deployment where the HSM sits in your tenancy — that's the typical BYOK flow. some customers we've seen have asked for offline key custody proofs; that's escalatable but needs legal signoff.
[04:15] Marco: about SLAs — what is the p99/p95 baseline and credits? we have an internal SLA remediation flow that requires measurable SLOs.
[04:28] Maya: our standard Dedicated SLA has 99.9% availability with credits on sustained breaches; the exact metric definitions are in the SLA exhibit we'll attach. for latency p95 numbers it's workload dependent, but Liam will bring p95 targets from similar customers.
[04:45] Liam: to add — with prefix caching and continuous batching enabled, we often see p95 generation latency under 250 ms on small- to medium-size models; larger seq lengths increase that. i'll share a short benchmark sheet.
[05:12] Nina (Cloud): network question — do you require VPC peering or can we use private link? we have strict egress rules.
[05:22] Liam: both are supported. PrivateLink or VPC peering are common; PrivateLink reduces broad network scope but has a slightly different NAT behavior. we'll recommend setup in the network preflight doc.
[05:40] Aisha: the MSA DPA redlines — we already marked three asks: data deletion confirmation window (30 vs 90 days), breach notification timing (24 vs 72 hours), and liability carveouts if model outputs cause downstream losses.
[05:58] Maya: 30 days deletion is a common ask; we can see whether 30 is possible for certain hosted logs but for backups there's sometimes a 90-day bound. we'll call that out in the tracker and propose a middle-ground for certain artifacts.
[06:15] Marco: for breach notification, 72 hours is what our legal team wants. is 24 hours realistic for you?
[06:23] Liam: 24 hours is aggressive, but we can commit to initial triage within 24 hours and a full notification within 72. we'll map that language so legal has something actionable.
[06:35] Priya: on pricing approval — what does the procurement path look like? do we need a PO up front for pilot?
[06:42] Maya: for pilots we can sometimes do a limited PO or MSA with a capped usage commitment. often we do a 90-day pilot with an estimated spend and monthly invoicing. we'll tailor the billing path per your finance policy.
[07:00] Derek: security checklist — do you provide audit logs per token or per request? our compliance wants high fidelity for retention and sampling.
[07:10] Liam: we have token-level cost breakdowns and per-request traces in the console; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. note that token-level exports may include hashed prompts depending on DPA settings.
[07:28] Aisha: competitor check — our platform team asked if we looked at LambdaCloud and VeloxAI, mostly for on-prem cost comparisons. any notes?
[07:36] Maya: both have strengths, LambdaCloud has tight pricing on spot capacity; VeloxAI offers deep on-prem integrations. Redwood differentiates on unified runtime and built-in rollout tooling — we'll send a short competitive notes doc.
[07:55] Marco: legal question — if we ask for audit rights including source code escrow for a subset of the runtime, is that an immediate blocker?
[08:06] Maya: escrow is a heavier ask; we've done it for strategic customers under separate escrow arrangements. not necessarily a blocker but will add time to onboarding.
[08:18] Priya: can you run an example fee calc with egress scenarios? network egress has been a hidden cost for other providers.
[08:26] Liam: yes, egress is usually metered per GB and can be material depending on throughput. i'll include three scenarios in the pricing worksheet — low, mid, and high egress.
[08:42] Aisha: timeline check — procurement needs the MSA redline and SOC2 by April 1 to keep our board timeline. can you hit that?
[08:51] Maya: we'll prioritize. SOC2 upload by March 31, and i'll send the MSA redline tracker by April 1.
[09:02] Marco: on SLA remedies, we may push for a service credit stack and an option for a termination right after two SLA breaches in a quarter. is that standard?
[09:12] Maya: termination rights are negotiable; many customers accept remedial plans and credits but termination for repeated breached is discussed on a case-by-case. we'll show precedent language.
[09:28] (cross-talk)
[09:35] Nina: technical preflight — can Liam share a sample VPC peering diagram and the NAT ports?
[09:42] Liam: yes, that's in the network preflight doc; i'll attach a picture of port lists and suggested CIDR ranges.
[09:55] Derek: encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted customer-side if we use private? and what about KV cache encryption?
[10:04] Liam: model artifacts at rest are encrypted; with customer-managed keys you can control wrapping. KV cache is encrypted at rest and in transit, but the keying model depends on deployment mode. we'll demonstrate key flows in the next deep dive.
[10:22] Maya: ok we'll wrap up with explicit next steps. quick recap: Redwood sends MSA redline tracker, SOC2, pricing worksheet, and Liam supplies network preflight and pilot latency/benchmark. StratusPay will confirm FinOps lane and internal legal criteria.
[10:45] Aisha: thanks. please mark the pricing worksheet to show committed vs burst and the egress assumptions.
[10:52] Maya: will do. any final quick q?
[11:00] Marco: none from me.
[11:02] Priya: just ensure invoices for pilot are monthly and itemized.
[11:06] Maya: noted. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule the SE-led deep dive for next week.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (Redwood Dedicate, K-V cash instead of KV cache). Recording aligns with 56 minute duration, some sections truncated by noise suppression.
